title: How I Prepared And Cracked The Citibank Internship Interview - Jay Baviskar, IIM Kozhikode
description: Getting into Citibank and charting a career path as a future investment banker is a highly sought after position by various b-school students. In this highly detailed interview, Jay describes the complex and thorough process that he underwent to get selected for a summer internship and with Citibank. Here's how he did it!  #MBASummerInternship #InternshipAtCitiBank #IIMKozhikode  Summary of the video: Wondering how Citibank hires top talent? What is the complete procedure that the company follows to hire Summer Interns from India's top business schools? How many rounds of selection exist, and how do you prepare yourself in such a competitive environment for a position with Citibank? And finally, what are the things to keep in mind before and during the internship?  In this video, Jay Baviskar, a part of IIM Kozhikode’s PGP Class of 2020, describes how he made it to Citibank as a Summer Intern. After graduating as an urban planning engineer, and gaining work experience for a few months, Jay got into IIM K, hoping to advance his career. He talks about zeroing in on Citibank as his preferred company and how he prepared for summer internship interviews as a whole. He describes his interview experience with Citibank in detail, and shares his ecstasy upon being selected. Jay shares with us his unforgettable selection process.   Further, Jay shares his pre-internship prep and tells us how he kept up with news and trends before the internship started. He takes us through the salient points of his internship and tells us his final project. He gives some invaluable advice on how to make your internship matter.   Here are a few key takeaways from Jay's interview that one must keep in mind: 1. Study the basics of all the subjects just before summer interviews. 2. Be aware of the news about companies performing well in each sector. 3. Company research is very important. 4. Make it a point to learn more about the company you’ll be working at in the lead up to your internship. 5. Make your past experience count by working in core subjects to ensure how you can maximise your interview performance.

asr.full_text: Subscribe to our channel and press the bell icon to never miss an update. My project revolved majorly around data visualizations and representatives and analytics When we were on campus, we had many things going on. We had the academics going on, we had many things going on. We had the academics going on. We had placement preparations going o. So it became a bit tedious and a bit hectic to manage, but eventually we got used to it. As a particular field of specialization, I didn't have anything in mind. It wasn't a general thing, because I didn't have any hardcore background or any such field. So it was a mixed prep, which was going on, plus the subjects here, which we are taught in our first term, they covered almost every aspect of of management. So we were introduced to marketing, operations, some kind of finance. And it was an overall preparation going on and not focused on a particular field. So as far as the preparation for companies was concerned, I didn't have a particular list in mind, but it was a preparation of all the subjects, a holistic preparation. Like for marketing, I used to study the basic concepts. Even for finance, like I kept myself abreast of the news of various companies which were performing good and which we got to speak on campus. That's why the preparation involved reading about these companies what new trends are there in the industry. Which companys are innovating which company is leading in a particular field so these kinds of things i usually read so that i was aware of who was there that was performing well in the industry One thing I like about Citi is that they are a leader and they always keep innovating and they're all very dynamic group if you see in the banking sector So they are a leader in many of their aspects, they were kind of the first people to introduce credit cards in India. Even now they have a very dynamic system which is like challenging but also which has its advantages. So that's why I preferred Citi. Also it has a global Expanse so working with people from different teams even in India there are many people are in different different fields, even in India, there are many people in many different fields which they take from so it has, in general, a holistic experience to learn from different people. So, that's why I chose City. Firstly, I spoke to the seniors, so seniors were all assigned to different projects so all of their learnings were very useful when they were working on projects which I read about online then. Also, I read more about City in the News Also, I visited their website because they have a lot of upcoming projects which are basically trending in the industry so, maybe it is robotic process automation or such related projects which are not very common but they are bringing a big change in the finance and the banking industry in general I read more about it, I spoke to seniors, I spoke to some of my friends who are at CITY and In general news as I said on the website, that helps me a lot in knowing where CITY stands and what I should read more about. So the process of CITY involved group discussions followed by a personal interview, so in group discussion also they gave us a topic which was related to banking industry, so the group, the GED went well, we are all from the first year, we had just barely completed a term on campus! So, we had some basic knowledge about what finance is, what companies do and by extra reading which gave me a bit of knack over what city is having an expertise in! so even during the personal interview I spoke about about what Citi is doing and I answered the questions accordingly. Some basic terms of finance which we usually covered in the term 1. So the interview majorly revolved around those things. I feel that I was quite abreast with Citi's work and I answered some of those questions keeping those things in mind or bringing those things in mind or bringing those points in perspective, so that's why I felt that that might have given me an advantage during the interview. After our first term, during our second and third term we were introduced to new subjects and some of them were hard-core subjects like financial management and all so while studying those subjects I kept a perspective of what Citi is doing in those things. Also, I kept on reading more about CITI and also about various technology and other banks. That helped me to develop the skill of where CITI is, its' competitors are.. and how I could contribute to CITI during my project. We weren't told about our projects prior, but I had a brief overview of where all the banking industry in general is. So those things helped me in working at Citi. Also the various… using various technologies that Citi uses, the various software which I had learned during my first year. Software is majorly included Microsoft Excel, Power Point and maybe working on SharePoint. So these things if I could bring them, or use them in during my internship at CITI, I felt that I could contribute more towards my internship as well as the organization. First day in CITI was in Hotel Trident in BKC. So that's where all of our 636 interns had gathered and the first day was majorly talking to people, talking to people, students from different colleges, talking to the HR team, talking to business leaders, there was a lot of sessions lined up for us and they were quite engaging so we had group activities. They also had a photo session with the CHRO of Citigroup. It was a nice experience that way. Also during our lunch and dinner we used to talk with people from different colleges so what's the scenario there how do they look at what are the interactions which they do the senior-junior interactions which we have also what backgrounds do we come from so it was a more of a team-building exercise which we had with among 66 of us. The business leaders obviously told us about what Citi is doing in their particular sector and what new trends are there and how we could contribute. The one day was not most project-specific, but it was in general related to Citi Group. That gave us an overview of the business functions of Citigroup. I was assigned to the first international financial centre at BKCA for Citigroup and my project was revolved around data visualisations, representations and analytics using various software. Also, I had another component of my project which was automating some of the manual tasks which were being performed at SETI SETA has a lot of jargons used, so day one was bit overwhelming but in course of time I spoke to people of different, so initially it wasn't a very like I know this, I know that, I know that so I had kept asking questions to the people of different teams which I was working with. And the culture of Citi was very accommodating and everyone answered all our questions even though it was a busy schedule. They would maybe postpone our appointment but they would answer our questions early. It was a very nice experience learning about the map, banking jargons and how the city works, how the functioning of the city is, so I felt I could do the project but they Learning about math, bank jargons and how city works. So the project, I could do it but I needed help from other people definitely from what the hardcore process of city was. It was a nice experience to learn about my project and interact with different people while working. During the final presentation, we presented all our work and people who we were managed by were quite busy so sometimes we didn't have weekly updates with them so we had to ourselves go and talk to them in the final presentation it was majorly regarding how implementable our projects were given the difficulties which we had which the projects had in maybe accessing data and all so the implementation was a big factor which they questioned us regarding that and the processes which we gave how useful would that be in reducing the time which people invested on maybe reducing the manual touchpoints or automating it so that people could work more rather than spending more of their time here. Plus, the things which we learnt they were a big plus-point for me. I spoke to different teams, I learned new skills, so that not only helped me during my internship but also when I joined my college and my second year.
